sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2006. Torricelli languages. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language & Linguistics, 2nd ed. Oxford: Elsevier.
sources.note: Family-level only: 'although stress is frequently contrastive, reports of tonal differences are rare' in Torricelli languages; nothing specific to Yahang.
Consonant and vowel charts attributed to Foley 2018; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: ELAR deposit 0550 'Documentation of Heyo [auk], a Torricelli language of Papua New Guinea' (Thomas Diaz, University at Buffalo); item yahang001 'Some words in Yahang', 2018-10-20, speaker Alois Wambre, hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0014-0171-C.
sources.note: Audio word elicitation only (restricted 'User' access); deposit description has no phonological information on Yahang.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. Yahang Swadesh List (archive.org rosettaproject_rhp_swadesh-1, 2010; data = Laycock 1968).
sources.note: Wordlist only; a single form carries an acute (wətə́f 'stone'), no statement.

sources.citation: Cooper, Gregory. 1981. A sociolinguistic survey of Beli, Yahang and Laeko-Libuat. In Richard Loving (ed.), Sociolinguistic surveys of Sepik languages (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 29), 141-161. Ukarumpa: SIL.
sources.note: Nothing. 21 pp. read in full (scanned): language use, attitudes, Tok Pisin literacy test, lexicostatistics (Yahang 60% cognate with Heyo, 30% Siliput); no phonology, no wordlist printed.

sources.citation: Laycock, D.C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (PL C-38), 767-780. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.767
sources.note: Nothing. General Torricelli phonology paragraph (p.769: three places of articulation, no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, many fricatives) has no stress remark; Yahang appears only in the classification list (Maimai Family, pop. 1001).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification (PL B-25). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 35 Yahang (Rurihi'ip, Ruruhip, Ya'unk): villages Engiep, Imbiyip, Kalem, Maimai, Teremes, Wombiu; 'see Laycock (1968:22)'.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 197-432. De Gruyter Mouton. (Maimai section with Tables 104-105, Yahang consonant/vowel phonemes.)
